text: AP reported that Democrats will win control of the U.S. House, retaking it from Republicans; LEX18 published the AP call at 1:27 AM ET.
Decision Desk HQ projected Democrat Abdul El-Sayed the winner of Michigan's U.S. Senate race; AP had not called the race as of 2:19 AM ET.
source: Decision Desk HQ via Mediaite (Yahoo News); AP via KSTP

text: Alaska's U.S. Senate race is uncalled with about 27% of precincts reporting; ranked-choice tabulation, if needed, is set for Nov. 18, KTOO reported.
AP reported Democrat Troy Jackson won Maine's U.S. Senate race over Republican Sen. Susan Collins; AP's report was published at 1:07 AM ET.
AP projected Democrat Peggy Flanagan the winner of Minnesota's U.S. Senate race over Republican Michele Tafoya, Scripps News reported at 12:10 AM ET.
AP reported that Democrat Tanya Miller won Georgia's attorney general race; AP's report was published at 10:50 PM ET.
AP called Georgia's Amendment 3 (9-1-1 fund) as approved at 8:09 PM ET and Amendment 2 (nonpartisan probate judges) as approved at 8:55 PM ET.
AP reported that Democrats have retaken control of the U.S. Senate in a report published at 11:40 PM ET.
AP reported Democrat Adam Hamilton defeated Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas's U.S. Senate race.
AP projected Democrat Josh Turek the winner of Iowa's open U.S. Senate seat over Republican Ashley Hinson, Iowa Capital Dispatch reported.
Republican Sen. Susan Collins conceded Maine's U.S. Senate race to Democrat Troy Jackson, the Portland Press Herald reported.
AP called Ohio's U.S. Senate special election for Democrat Sherrod Brown over Republican Sen. Jon Husted, KSHB reported at 11:13 PM ET.
AP called Texas's U.S. Senate race for Democrat James Talarico over Republican Ken Paxton, NewsChannel 5 reported at 11:05 PM ET.
Decision Desk HQ projected that Democrats will win control of the U.S. House, Bloomberg reported.
AP called Georgia's lieutenant governor race for Democrat Josh McLaurin, WSB-TV reported at 10:47 PM ET.
AP reported that Democrat Penny Brown Reynolds won Georgia's secretary of state race; AP's report was published at 10:40 PM ET.
AP projected Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms the winner of Georgia's governor race; FOX 5 Atlanta reported the AP call at 9:24 PM ET.
NBC News projected Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms the winner of Georgia's governor race shortly after 9:15 PM ET.
source: NBC News; call time per Washington Examiner

text: AP called New Hampshire's U.S. Senate race for Democrat Chris Pappas; AP's report of the call was published at 8:25 PM ET.
AP called North Carolina's U.S. Senate race for Democrat Roy Cooper at 8:23 PM ET.
AP called Georgia's U.S. Senate race for Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff at 7:55 PM ET.
Republican John E. Sununu conceded New Hampshire's U.S. Senate race to Democrat Chris Pappas by 8:15 PM ET, the Boston Globe reports.
Georgia's first returns are in: ABC News showed 44% of the expected vote counted in the U.S. Senate race as of 7:59 PM ET.
Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said he expects Georgia's early-vote results to be uploaded by 8 p.m. ET tonight.
source: Georgia Secretary of State via ABC News

text: At 10 a.m. ET, Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said more than 300,000 Georgians had voted so far today; his office expects over 1 million by day's end.
source: Georgia Secretary of State via WTOC

text: Fulton County will re-scan about 1,000 early-voting ballots from two scanners taken out of service; Raffensperger said this won't delay any race results.
Georgia polls are open from 7 AM to 7 PM ET. Anyone in line at 7 PM can still vote.
AP will declare winners in Georgia's Senate, governor and other statewide races, plus all three constitutional amendments.
On Oct. 27, Georgia's Secretary of State said he expects results to be clear before midnight tonight.
No Libertarians made Georgia's statewide ballot, so each statewide race has two candidates and a December runoff is unlikely.
Georgia passed its 2022 midterm early-voting record: 2,294,275 in-person early votes as of Oct. 29, with one day left.
